claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures that for infants (especially newborns), having eyes partially or completely closed is acceptable. All dimensions are properly represented.

source_spans.quote: It is acceptable if the infant's eyes, particularly a newborn's, are partially or completely closed;

claim_results.rationale: The claim faithfully reflects that the infant's head may be discreetly supported with white/off-white backing.

source_spans.quote: The infant's head may be discreetly supported, e.g., a car seat with a white or off-white blanket behind the child.

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly reflects that head tilt is acceptable for infants.

source_spans.quote: Head tilt is acceptable for infants;

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the prohibition against a parent's face appearing in an infant's photograph.

source_spans.quote: A parent’s face cannot be in the photograph of the infant.

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly details the mandatory requirement to request a new photograph if submitted requirements are unmet.

source_spans.quote: You must request a new photograph if the photograph submitted does not meet the following requirements:

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately reflects that passport photographs must be in color.

source_spans.quote: The photograph must be in color;

claim_results.rationale: The claim properly captures the recommendation regarding timing within six months and satisfactory identification.

source_spans.quote: The photograph should be taken within six months of submitting the application, be a good likeness of and satisfactorily identify the applicant at the time of the application (see 22 CFR 51.26).

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the permission for changes in hairstyle or facial hair provided it remains a good likeness.

source_spans.quote: A photograph showing a change in hairstyle or facial hair from the identification document submitted is acceptable if it still is a good likeness of the applicant;

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly reflects that the photograph must be free of material damage.

source_spans.quote: The photograph must be free of material damage:

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately defines material damage and includes the alternatives specified.

source_spans.quote: Material damage is any damage to the facial area that makes the photograph no longer a good likeness of the applicant (e.g., creases, large holes, and large smudges) or impedes the functioning of facial recognition (damage in the area of the eyes);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately defines immaterial damage according to the source.

source_spans.quote: Immaterial damage is any damage to the background, and non-material damage to the facial area (e.g., staple holes).

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly captures the rule that immaterial damage is acceptable.

source_spans.quote: Immaterial damage is acceptable;

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly conveys that the applicant is not required to sign the photograph.

source_spans.quote: The applicant does not need to sign the photograph, as this often causes creases or smudges;

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately represents the requirement for acceptance agents to sign the back of hand-carry application photographs.

source_spans.quote: For hand-carry applications, the acceptance agent signs the back of the photograph.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately conveys that an application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph if a defect becomes apparent upon printing.

source_spans.quote: Consequently, the passport application may be returned to adjudication to request a new photograph even though the photograph appeared acceptable.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately conveys the prohibition of eyeglasses except when medically unremovable.

source_spans.quote: Eyeglasses are not acceptable unless they cannot be removed for medical reasons, e.g., the applicant has recently had ocular surgery and the eyeglasses are necessary to protect the applicant’s eyes.

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately sets out the requirement to request a signed medical statement when eyeglasses cannot be removed for medical reasons.

source_spans.quote: A medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner must be requested in these rare circumstances.

claim_results.rationale: The claim correctly details that frames must not cover the eye(s) when eyeglasses are accepted for medical reasons.

source_spans.quote: The frames of the eyeglasses must not cover the eye(s);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures the prohibition against glare obscuring the eye(s).

source_spans.quote: There must not be glare on eyeglasses that obscures the eye(s);

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately captures that shadows or refraction obscuring the eye(s) are prohibited.

source_spans.quote: There must not be shadows or refraction from the eyeglasses that obscure the eye(s); and

claim_results.rationale: The claim accurately states that dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement indicates they are required.

source_spans.quote: Dark or tinted lenses are permitted if the medical statement also indicates that they are required.

claim_results.rationale: C0021 accurately captures the recommendation and conditions for issuing a limited-validity passport with endorsement 46 when eyeglasses are temporarily needed and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.

source_spans.quote: A limited-validity passport using endorsement 46 should be issued when the medical circumstance that requires eyeglasses is temporary and the applicant has urgent or emergency travel.

claim_results.rationale: C0022 correctly represents the guidance that an applicant's facial expression should be natural.

source_spans.quote: The applicant’s expression should be natural.

claim_results.rationale: C0023 correctly captures both the permission for normal, unexaggerated smiles and the exclusion of unusual expressions and squinting.

source_spans.quote: Normal, unexaggerated smiles are acceptable, but unusual expressions and squinting are not.

claim_results.rationale: C0024 faithfully preserves the permission to accept photographs lacking a natural/unexaggerated expression when due to physical or mental disabilities.

source_spans.quote: Applicants with physical or mental disabilities, including loss of muscle control (e.g., age-related degeneration or because of a medical condition such as Bell's Palsy), may not be able to produce a natural or unexaggerated expression.
You may accept a photograph without a natural or unexaggerated expression in these circumstances.

claim_results.rationale: C0025 accurately conveys the requirement/recommendation that both eyes be visible and open, noting the infant exception.

source_spans.quote: Both of the applicant’s eyes should also be visible and open in the photograph (see the exception for infants in 8 FAM 402.1-1).

claim_results.rationale: C0026 precisely reflects the rule allowing acceptance of a photo if the applicant cannot open one or both eyes due to a medical condition.

source_spans.quote: If the applicant is unable to open one or both eyes because of a medical condition, you may accept the photograph.

claim_results.rationale: C0027 properly covers the recommendation to request a signed medical statement in rare cases where closed eyes or exaggerated expressions are unlikely to be medically caused.

source_spans.quote: In rare cases, if it is unlikely that the closed eye(s) or exaggerated expression are because of a medical condition, you should request a medical statement signed by a medical professional/health practitioner.

claim_results.rationale: C0028 captures the actor, modality, and action directing specified agency and consular personnel to refer photo-less applications to supervisors.

source_spans.quote: Applications received without photographs:

Processing and communications/customer service personnel at passport agencies/centers or consular section personnel should refer applications without photographs to their supervisor for guidance on processing passport applications received without photographs;

claim_results.rationale: C0029 accurately states the prohibition against accepting DS-11 or DS-82 forms without photographs at the public counter.

source_spans.quote: You must not accept a form DS-11 or form DS-82 received without a photograph at the public counter.

claim_results.rationale: C0030 correctly reflects the mandatory requirement for passport specialists to suspend DS-11 applications received from an acceptance facility without a photo.

source_spans.quote: Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-11 received without a photograph from an acceptance facility.

claim_results.rationale: C0031 accurately retains the requirement that the applicant re-execute Form DS-11 when it was received without a photograph from an acceptance facility.

source_spans.quote: The applicant must re-execute the form DS-11 (see IRL 975-04);

claim_results.rationale: C0032 accurately sets forth the mandate for passport specialists to suspend Form DS-82 or DS-5504 received without a photograph.

source_spans.quote: Passport specialists must suspend a form DS-82 or form DS-5504 received without a photograph (see IRL 1000-05 and IRL 1018-14).
